messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Production kv-cache group 'tp-shard-a' reporting sustained growth in KV cache objects + increased continuous batching rate. Multiple GPUs entering OOM/paging, NCCL stalls observed by metrics. Paging count spiked 6x in last 5m. Auto-mitigation triggered: draining batch queue. @oncall please acknowledge. :rotating_light:

alex.h: acked. Are we seeing errors in frontend? Any 5xx spikes?

ben.m: I see 502 spikes for a handful of tenants (ingest path). Tail latency up to 20-45s on affected shards.

jyoti.s: Confirming NCCL stall traces on TP group. Logs show repeated NCCL op timeouts during all-reduce when cache refill happens.

samir: Looks like continuous batching frequency doubled after a config rollout 03:40. Could be a regression in debounce logic that causes runaway small batches.

maria.p: Paging metrics show GPU memory pressure from KV entries — sizes increased per-key after a recent kv-serialization change. Possibly larger tensors stored in cache.

ops-bot: mitigation suggestion: reduce continuous batch window + scale down batch workers. CLI to set: 
```
redwoodctl config set kv.continuous_batch_window_ms 50 --env prod
redwoodctl scale deployment kv-batcher --replicas 2 --env prod
```

ben.m: I'm going to pause continuous batching on the affected pool now. Patching policy: set continuous_batch_enabled=false for pool tp-shard-a.

alex.h: Do it and route traffic to fallback model variant with smaller kv footprint. Add circuit-breaker for retries.

ben.m: Ran disable command: `redwoodctl patch pool tp-shard-a --set continuous_batch_enabled=false` 
Response: success. Immediate drop in new batch rate.

jyoti.s: After disable, NCCL stall rate dropped ~70% but we still see uneven tensor partitioning across GPUs causing a few lingering slow requests.

samir: For a fast rollback, rolling back the serialization change may help but that's riskier. Instead plan: hotfix to cap KV entry size during cache insert and enforce shard-aligned padding to avoid rounding mismatch across TP slices.

maria.p: Oncall note: affected customers A, C, D saw 5-30s tail latencies, 3 tenants had 502s. CS has been pinged.

cs-lead: Noted. We'll open support cases and send interim status to impacted customers: "We're mitigating a KV cache-induced performance regression; we've applied a temporary batch config to reduce impact and are working on a code hotfix."

ben.m: Quick mitigation plan executed: 1) disable continuous batching on tp-shard-a (done), 2) scale up fallback pool to absorb traffic, 3) apply cache-insert size cap.

ops-bot: Commands used: 
```
redwoodctl scale pool fallback-pool --replicas 4 --env prod
redwoodctl feature-flag set kv.size_cap 128MB --env prod
```

jyoti.s: Pushed a staging patch that enforces per-shard slice alignment to avoid NCCL all-reduce size discrepancies. Need one more test before prod rollout.

samir: Also backfilled an immediate metric: per-GPU kv_entry_byte_histogram and shard_slice_size mismatch gauge. Adding alert: shard_slice_size_variance > 5% -> paging-oncall.

alex.h: Can someone capture a short incident summary for handoff? Ben, please lead for next hour.

ben.m: Taking lead. Handoff note: Incident focused on kv cache growth + continuous batching regression causing NCCL stalls on TP group. Immediate mitigations applied (batching disabled, fallback scaled, size cap). Customer impact: increased latency and some 502s. Next step: prod-safe hotfix for shard-aligned padding + revert serialization change if tests fail.

maria.p: I'll coordinate CS messages and collect tenant logs. Sending draft status update to impacted tenants in #customer-updates after we confirm the cap is stable.

cs-lead: Include ETA: 1-2 hours for hotfix rollout, will update if things change.

ben.m: Running canary of the alignment patch to one shard group now. Command: `deployctl canary --app kv-runtime --image sha:abcd1234 --shard tp-shard-b --env prod`

jyoti.s: Canary passed basic NCCL sanity. No stalls for 15m, shard slice sizes aligned. Preparing prod rollout plan with 5-min canaries per shard.

samir: Added follow-up tickets: INF-3421 (root cause: batch debounce regression), INF-3422 (kv-serialization size regression), INF-3423 (per-shard metric alerts), INF-3424 (postmortem and customer RCA).

ben.m: Rolling out patch to remaining shards now in a staggered manner. Monitoring GPU paging and NCCL error rate dashboards.

ops-bot: Reminder: escalate to SEV-level if >10% tenants see errors after 60m. Currently at 2.1% impacted.

alex.h: Good. Keep updates in this thread. If anyone makes a config change, paste the exact CLI and confirmation response.

maria.p: Update: CS sent initial status to tenants. One large customer requested a postmortem — we'll prioritize.

jyoti.s: After full rollout, NCCL stalls are back to baseline and GPU paging reduced to pre-incident levels. Cache object median size reduced ~40% after cap.

ben.m: Closing mitigation: continuous batching remains disabled for tp-shard-a until infra patch is part of stable. Will re-enable with stricter rate limits once we validate.

samir: Postmortem items: root cause summary to include (1) config rollback allowed runaway continuous batching frequency, (2) kv serialization change increased per-key bytes, (3) sharding alignment bug in TP path led to uneven all-reduce sizes causing NCCL stalls under pressure.

ben.m: Marking incident status: Mitigated -> monitoring. Transferring to post-incident owner: samir.

alex.h: Thanks everyone. Great quick coordination. :clap:
